goal: Classify a Calculator protocol request into its answer kind, so a malformed, unsupported or out-of-range request is never answered with a number.

app.name: calculator-protocol
app.title: Calculator protocol
app.purpose: Classify one Calculator protocol request, from its protocol version, its operation, whether the right operand is zero and whether the exact result fits a signed 64-bit integer, as ok or as the typed error the reference product answers.

fields.name: version
fields.means: the protocol version the request names; the product speaks version 1

fields.name: operation
fields.means: the operation name; other is any name the protocol does not define, such as mod

fields.name: range
fields.means: whether the exact mathematical result lies within the signed 64-bit range

rules.why: src/Calculator.lex.tex: decodeRequest refuses any version but 1 with ProtocolError UnsupportedVersion (vector 2 add 1 2)
src/Calculator.lex.tex: parseOperation knows only Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide; anything else is ProtocolError UnknownOperation (vector 1 mod 1 2)
src/Calculator.lex.tex: calculate answers CalculatorError DivisionByZero for a zero divisor (vector 1 divide 1 0)
src/Calculator.lex.tex: checkedResult answers CalculatorError Overflow outside the i64 range (vectors at 9223372036854775807 and -9223372036854775808)

app.otherwiseWhy: src/Calculator.lex.tex: calculate_correct proves the exact result is returned when it is in range

properties.why: a division by zero has no result
a result outside i64 is never wrapped or truncated
an unsupported version is never interpreted as version 1
an undefined operation is a typed protocol error

stakeholders.name: Calculator user
stakeholders.text: Enters two operands and an operation in the Pages view and needs an exact result or a typed error, never a wrapped number.

stakeholders.name: Service operator
stakeholders.text: Runs the A/B service releases and needs every protocol error typed and covered by a negative vector.

components.name: Calculator service release
components.text: The A and B service releases prismpm pushes, deploys and rolls back.

threats.name: Silent overflow
threats.text: An out-of-range sum or product is wrapped and answered as ok.

control.name: Checked result
control.text: A result beyond i64 is answered overflow.

evidence.reference: UOR-Foundation/calculator-example src/Calculator.lex.tex acceptance vectors at the i64 bounds

threats.name: Division by zero answered
threats.text: A zero divisor yields a number or a trap instead of a typed error.

control.name: Typed division error
control.text: A zero divisor is answered division-by-zero.

threats.name: Version downgrade
threats.text: A client sends another protocol version hoping it is read as version 1.

quality.text: Each of the four Operation constructors is a value of the operation field.
quality.measureText: Operation constructors of src/Calculator.lex.tex the app distinguishes.

quality.text: Every CalculatorError and every ProtocolError but MalformedRequest, which the decoder answers invalid, is an answer.
quality.measureText: Error constructors with no answer and no invalid refusal.
